- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope sharply in next 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 2–5% in next period; if below, increase by 2–5%.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending down; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment lag” error.
- For 30d horizon, if last 3 days show strong negative sentiment + price decline, model often misses bottom; forecast should be 1–3% below true low for next 3 periods.
